title: Determine if Two Strings Are Close Problem

content.problemStatement:
Two strings are considered "close" if you can make them identical
using any number of these two operations, in any order: swap the
positions of any two existing characters, or replace every occurrence
of one existing character with another existing character (and vice
versa).

**Determine whether `word1` and `word2` are close.**
constraints: word1 and word2 consist only of lowercase English letters
operations may be applied any number of times, in any order
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: swapping characters can turn abc into bca directly, since they use the same letters
different lengths can never be made equal
both use the letters a, b, c with counts that can be matched up: {1,3,2} and {1,3,2}

code.Python3:
# Time:  O(n)
# Space: O(1)

import collections


class Solution(object):
    def closeStrings(self, word1, word2):
        """
        :type word1: str
        :type word2: str
        :rtype: bool
        """
        if len(word1) != len(word2):
            return False 
        
        cnt1, cnt2 = collections.Counter(word1), collections.Counter(word2)   # Reuse of keys
        return set(cnt1.iterkeys()) == set(cnt2.iterkeys()) and \
               collections.Counter(cnt1.itervalues()) == collections.Counter(cnt2.itervalues())
